item.title: Alabama Says TikTok to Pay Up to $300 Million for Kid Safety
item.description: Alabama’s attorney general said TikTok has agreed to pay up to $300 million and adopt new user protection measures to settle the state’s child-safety lawsuit that was set for a jury trial to begin Monday.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Fearn

item.title: Markets Rise as AI, Oil & Treasury Yields Drive the Week
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management Executive Director Katerina Simonetti, BMO Chief FX Strategist Mark McCormick, Jefferies Managing Director & Equity Research Analyst David Katz, Yale University Jackson Institute for Global Affairs Senior Fellow Stephen Roach, Citi Wealth Head of Portfolio Construction & Analytics Olaolu Aganga, Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson, Georgetown Institute of International Economic Law Visiting Scholar Peter Harrell, & Keeneland President & CEO Shannon Arvin. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Harrell: US-China Lack of Deliverables Was as Expected
item.description: Peter Harrell says that the key dynamic is not which country has the upper hand, but that both China and the United States have meaningful leverage: the U.S. through tariffs, export controls, semiconductors, the dollar and AI technology, and China through rare earths, specialty chemicals, and manufacturing scale. Harrell says this mutual leverage helps explain the recent emphasis on “strategic stability” and why both countries may want to ease tensions for now while they work to reduce their dependence on each other. He speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Patterson: AI Is Crowding Out Demand for US Treasuries
item.description: Rebecca Patterson, Former Chief Investment Strategist at Bridgewater and Senior Fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, discusses her broad read on market action. The discussion is framed around whether recent moves in bonds, equities, commodities, and energy are telling the same economic story or whether one market is more predictive than the others. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Katerina Simonetti Discusses Risk-Off Positioning as Volatility Spikes
item.description: Katerina Simonetti, Executive Director at Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Investments, discusses how to think about markets amid this year’s crosscurrents and whether a risk-off approach is still appropriate. Simonetti highlights a sharp jump in Treasury volatility, the biggest in a year, alongside a note that stocks are rising as oil retreats on hopes of a U.S.-Iran deal. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China's Economy Unbalanced, AI Deal Hard to Envision, Stephen Roach Says
item.description: Stephen Roach, Yale University Jackson Institute for Global Affairs senior fellow and former chairman of Morgan Stanley Asia, says President Donald Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping left many unresolved questions about tariffs, technology restrictions, rare earth leverage and Taiwan, even as both sides appeared to project some stability. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI’s Models Accessed Public US Census, SEC Data
item.description: OpenAI’s artificial intelligence models accessed publicly available information from US government websites, including those of the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz, Jeff Stone and Jake Bleiberg

item.title: Microsoft Rises as It Unifies Copilot AI | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Isabelle Lee, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Accel Sees AI Opportunity Shifting to Applications
item.description: The AI spending boom is showing no signs of slowing down, but as billions pour into models, chips and data centers, investors are asking where the biggest returns will actually be. Accel Partner Matt Weigand, who focuses on late-stage technology investments including AI infrastructure, says the AI boom is the biggest technology cycle Silicon Valley has seen. He also discusses why open-source AI can grow alongside frontier labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI and why trust and safety are becoming key considerations when Accel decides which AI founders to back. He joins Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Goes Big on Compute, Microsoft Rethinks AI
item.description: Bloomberg’s Tim Stenovec breaks down Anthropic's $11.6 billion contract with Akamai for AI computing power, the largest deal in Akamai's history. Plus, President Donald Trump calls his meeting with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping "very productive" with little to show for it. And, Microsoft steps back from the race to build a personal chatbot by instead merging the consumer and workplace versions of its Copilot AI assistant into one. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump-Xi Optics Overshadow Substance, Gewirtz Says
item.description: Julian Gewirtz, Harvard Belfer Center fellow and former senior director for China and Taiwan Affairs at the White House National Security Council during the Biden administration, says President Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping delivered the positive optics Trump was seeking, but little visible progress on the major challenges dividing the US and China. He discusses unresolved tensions around trade, Iran, Russia, and Taiwan, as well as the intensifying AI race. He joins Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Love-Hate Relationship With AI Unfolding on Social Media
item.description:
It has been a head-spinning time of change for social media content creators as AI slop proliferates all over the Internet.
On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast recorded live at the Vermont Hollywood theater, Rachel Karten, author of the Link in Bio newsletter, and Taylor Lorenz, founder of User Mag, tell Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway why people love some genres of slop and what type of content audiences still prefer to be created by humans. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Justice Department Closes Investigation of CrowdStrike Deals
item.description: US prosecutors have closed an investigation into deals CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. made with a distributor without taking further action, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg

item.title: The Six-Year Journey Behind ‘Big Walk’
item.description: The delightful new co-op game started off as a pandemic fever dream
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: Bitget Hack Pushes North Korean Crypto Haul Past $1 Billion
item.description: A $357 million hack of crypto exchange Bitget on Thursday was likely carried out by North Korea-linked hackers, pushing the nation-state’s haul from digital-asset thefts above $1 billion this year, according to analytics firm Elliptic Enterprises Ltd.
item.dc:creator: Ben Weiss

item.title: Google DeepMind Exodus Sparks VC Frenzy for AI’s Next Big Thing
item.description: When a group of 15 Google DeepMind employees and alumni met for a breakfast this month in central London, the conversation quickly turned to how to raise money for an artificial intelligence startup.
item.dc:creator: Yazhou Sun, Mark Bergen and Shona Ghosh

item.title: Bill Gates Warns AI Powerful Enough to Lead to ‘a Billion Deaths’
item.description: Microsoft Corp. co-founder Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence is a “powerful enough” tool to kill off a substantial portion of humanity, joining a growing chorus of tech leaders and employees calling attention to AI’s existential risks.
item.dc:creator: Micah Barkley

item.title: Ex-Tinder Exec Debuts Rivet, a Dating App That Lets Strangers Play Matchmaker
item.description: A former Tinder executive launched a new dating app that invites the community to vote on strangers’ compatibility, putting a twist on courtship at a time when singles have grown exhausted with swiping.Rivet, which opens to US users on Thursday, relies on a pool of volunteer “matchers” who rate whether two given people might be compatible. The idea is to prioritize quality connections over quantity, giving daters just a few pre-vetted options at a time, founder and Chief Executive Officer Taru K
item.dc:creator: Samantha Kelly

item.title: Amazon Gets EU Scrutiny on Possible Seller Price Curbs
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. is under scrutiny from the European Union for potentially imposing unfair restrictions on firms selling on its platform.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Soper and Samuel Stolton

item.title: CORRECT: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Eyes Long Bets
item.description:
The man who transformed how urban India eats, dines, and shops, Deepinder Goyal built his food delivery startup Zomato into one of the country’s biggest consumer technology companies, Eternal. At the height of its success, Goyal stepped away from the day-to-day running of the company he built, to turn his attention to a very different set of challenges with a much longer horizon.
In an exclusive interview on his sprawling residence in Delhi, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with Goyal about the never-ending journeys of founders, his current pursuits, and his quest for a different kind of eternity.
